survivors.title: corpus_index.dashboard_stats runs its second SQL query outside the _read_cursor() lock — gap-4 use-after-close race
survivors.evidence:
The first query is correctly scoped: `with _read_cursor() as conn:` ... `rows = conn.execute(...).fetchall()` (lines 1487-1494). But the SECOND query reuses the same handle AFTER the `with` block has exited (the lock is released and the context manager has returned):

    1487  with _read_cursor() as conn:
    1488      rows = conn.execute(... GROUP BY book_code, kind ...).fetchall()
    ...
    1509  chap_rows = conn.execute(   # <-- OUTSIDE the `with`, _CONN_LOCK no longer held
    1510      "SELECT book_code, chapter, COUNT(*) ... GROUP BY book_code, chapter", book_codes
    1514  ).fetchall()

`_read_cursor`'s own docstring (lines 727-737) states the lock must span the WHOLE read so a concurrent invalidate()/rebuild()/_build_to() (each of which closes `_CACHED_CONN` under _CONN_LOCK) cannot pull the handle out from under an in-flight execute() — the gap-4 race under the ThreadingHTTPServer + the build ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=5). Here `conn` is the shared `_CACHED_CONN`. `gather_stats` (scripts/dashboard.py:91) calls this from the web /dashboard console (worker thread). A notes-file save on another thread → notes_io.atomic_write → _invalidate_corpus_index_if_notes_file → corpus_index.invalidate() closes `_CACHED_CONN` exactly in the window between line 1494's fetch and line 1509's execute → `sqlite3.ProgrammingError: Cannot operate on a closed database`, 500-ing the dashboard. I checked all 11 _read_cursor/query sites in corpus_index.py (lines 793,806,827,833,840,918,1036,1238,1381,1487,1509) and grepped for external connection() callers (none) — this is the ONLY site whose conn.execute escapes its `with _read_cursor()` block; the rest correctly do everything inside the `with`.
survivors.fix: Move the second query inside the existing `with _read_cursor() as conn:` block so both queries run while _CONN_LOCK is held by one cursor lease. Concretely, indent the `chap_rows = conn.execute(...).fetchall()` statement (lines 1509-1514) into the same `with` block as the first query (and keep `placeholders`/`book_codes` in scope). Fetch both result sets inside the one `with`, then process them after. This matches the contract the docstring states ("Fetch ALL rows inside the `with` — never let a lazy cursor escape") and the pattern every other query helper in the module already follows.
